titleEn: I Am Not Good with Boomerangs
titleEs: No soy bueno con los bumeranes

titleText.es: Tira bonus: lee las viñetas de la derecha hacia abajo.
titleText.en: Bonus strip: just read the rightmost panels straight down.
titleText.noteEn: The title text identifies an alternate bonus reading: the four panels in the rightmost column form a second sequence when read straight down.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: I am leaving; I am ending a romantic relationship
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Dejo is the present form of dejar used by the speaker. Dejar can mean leaving a thing somewhere; with a romantic partner as the person affected, it can mean ending the relationship.

example.en: Today I am leaving my partner.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone leaves or breaks up with a romantic partner?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of dejar for the person ending the relationship, then identify the partner. A short word such as me or te goes before the changed form of dejar.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With a named or stated partner, put a before that person: dejó a su pareja. With a short word, put it before dejar: me dejó, te dejo. Dejar changes for who ends the relationship and when; context separates this sense from leaving an object somewhere.

example.en: Marta broke up with her partner.

applications.explanationEn: Te identifies the familiar singular person affected, and dejo is the speaker's present form of dejar in its relationship-ending sense.
